transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, um, I hope I'm in the right place for this. It's probably not a huge deal, and I really don't want to waste your time, but... well, what really pushed me to come in is just how jumpy I've been at work lately. 

I'm a receptionist, so I'm used to noise, but recently... if a door slams, or even if someone just rolls a suitcase really fast across the lobby, I jump. And not just a little bit. It's like... like it's happening again. My heart starts pounding, and it takes me a minute or so just to get it back down and compose myself. 

I know it probably sounds silly to get so worked up over a suitcase, and I'm trying to handle it, but I just wanted to make sure I'm doing the right thing by getting it checked out. Does that make sense?
Can you tell me if you’ve been feeling more anxious or worried most days, even when there’s no obvious reason for it?

Oh, um, no. Not really. I hope I didn't make it sound like I'm just a nervous wreck all the time. I really don't want you to think I'm just sitting around worrying about everything, because I'm usually a pretty upbeat guy. 

If there's no loud noise or nothing sudden happens, I actually feel completely fine. I don't just get anxious out of nowhere. It's really only when something catches me off guard, like the suitcase thing I mentioned. Otherwise, I'm doing my best to just stay positive and focus on my job. 

Is that... does that help clarify things? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you find yourself constantly on guard, even in safe or familiar places, like you're always expecting something bad to happen?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I'm definitely not constantly on guard. Like, when I'm at home in my apartment, I feel completely safe. I'm not... I'm not sitting around waiting for the other shoe to drop or anything like that. 

I really try to keep a positive outlook, you know? I don't want you to think I'm paranoid or just jumping at shadows all day. It's really just those sudden loud noises at work that get to me. 

I hope that's a good sign? That I can still relax and feel safe at home, I mean. I'm really trying my best to handle things well, so... I hope that sounds like a normal reaction to you?
When you're startled by a loud noise and your heart starts pounding, does it feel like you're reliving a specific moment or memory that was frightening or upsetting?

Well, um... I guess, yeah, it does kind of feel like that. I really don't want to sound dramatic, because I know people go through much worse things, but... sometimes, out of nowhere, I'll just get this flash in my head. 

It's this picture of... of a guest at the hotel. He was really angry, and he leaned way over the counter and just shoved all the equipment toward me. It was a while ago, and I know I should probably be over it by now, but that image just pops up. Even when I'm just trying to answer a totally normal phone call and everything is fine. 

I try to just push it away and keep a smile on my face for the guests, you know? I hope that doesn't make me sound crazy or anything. Is it normal to still picture something like that when you're just trying to do your job?
Have you found yourself avoiding certain people, places, or situations because they remind you of that upsetting incident at work?

Well, um... I wouldn't say I'm avoiding my duties or anything like that. I'm definitely still doing my job, I promise! But, um... I guess I have been changing my route just a little bit. 

I've been taking the back hallway whenever I can. It's just... walking past that specific spot in the lobby where it happened, it kind of makes my chest tighten up, and I just want to get away from it. I still get everywhere I need to be on time, though! I'm not letting it ruin my schedule or anything. I just prefer the back way right now so I can stay focused and keep a good attitude. 

I hope that's okay? I mean, does that sound like a normal way to handle it, just for now? I really don't want it to seem like I'm hiding.

latest_inference.note: The patient described symptoms of re-experiencing a traumatic event (flashbacks), hyperarousal (being jumpy at loud noises), and avoidance (changing routes at work), which are consistent with Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (F43.10). Other candidates were ruled out based on absence of generalized anxiety (F41.9), panic attacks (F40.01), obsessive-compulsive features (F40.210), mood symptoms (F34.8), psychotic features (F20.6), depersonalization/derealization (F06.4), or dissociative amnesia (F44.7). The patient does not endorse symptoms inconsistent with F43.10, and the clinical picture aligns most closely with PTSD.
